items.title: Emin's My Bed
items.claim: Tracey Emin's My Bed was shortlisted for the Turner Prize in 1999. In 2014 it sold at auction. For approximately how much?
items.reveal:
Christie's London sold My Bed for around £2.5 million (with buyer's premium) on 1 July 2014.

The work was later loaned to the Tate by Count Christian Duerckheim.
items.why: Markets give surprising answers to questions about value in conceptual and autobiographical art.

items.title: Banksy's self-shredding
items.claim: In October 2018 a Banksy work partially shredded during a Sotheby's auction. What happened to the price after the stunt?

options.text: It sold for the auction price, then resold in 2021 for around £18.6 million
The buyer sued and won damages

items.reveal:
Originally hammered at around £1 million on 5 October 2018, the partially shredded work was renamed Love Is in the Bin and resold in October 2021 for around £18.6 million.

The shredder was concealed in the frame.
items.why: Critiques of art markets can become market assets themselves.

items.title: Kahlo's body of work
items.claim: Roughly what proportion of Frida Kahlo's known paintings are self-portraits?
items.reveal_title: Roughly one third of around 150 works
items.reveal:
Standard catalogues list around 150 paintings, of which approximately 55 are self-portraits. Kahlo wrote that she painted herself 'because I am so often alone, because I am the subject I know best'.

Her first US museum retrospective opened only in 1978, 24 years after her death.
items.why: Recognition timing shapes how an artist's body of work is constructed by curators and historians.
